summary.short: Sets the user-number and functionality thresholds that place online services in Category 1, 2A or 2B under the UK Online Safety Act 2023, which triggers additional duties under the Act. In force 27 February 2025.
summary.long: These regulations, made by the Secretary of State on Ofcom's advice and approved by both Houses of Parliament, define when regulated online services meet the threshold conditions for the Online Safety Act 2023 categories. Category 1 covers user-to-user services with more than 34 million average monthly active UK users and a content recommender system, or more than 7 million with a recommender system and a forward or share function. Category 2A covers search engines with more than 7 million users, except vertical search engines that search selected sources through API-based arrangements. Category 2B covers user-to-user services with more than 3 million users and a direct-messaging function. User numbers are the monthly mean over the six months before the month in which Ofcom's assessment begins. The duties attached to each category, and the assessment and register process, are set in the parent Act (sections 95-97), not in this instrument.

notes: Thresholds combine a user-number test with functionality tests (recommender system, forward or share, direct messaging), so services can also fall outside a category by changing features.
